html:
The Western Chalukya Empire ruled most of the western Deccan from 973 to 1189, with its capital at Kalyani in today's Karnataka. On the 1100 map it is at its height.

In 973 Tailapa II, a vassal, overthrew the last of the Rashtrakutas and revived the old Chalukya name. For a century the empire fought the Chola Empire for the rich lands of Vengi and the Tungabhadra, in wars that neither side won.

Its greatest king, Vikramaditya VI, ruled from 1076 to 1126. His court poet Bilhana wrote his life, and the jurist Vijnaneshwara wrote the Mitakshara, a commentary on Hindu law that courts used into modern times. Ornate temples rose at Lakkundi, Itagi and many other towns.

After 1150 vassals broke away. The Kalachuri Bijjala seized Kalyani, where Basava began the Lingayat movement as his minister. The empire's lands were then shared by the Hoysalas, the Yadavas and the Kakatiyas.
sum: The Western Chalukya Empire ruled most of the western Deccan from 973 to 1189, with its capital at Kalyani in today's Karnataka. On the 1100 map it is at its height.
